{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01RVt593AqaJTxRSFbEy5gQi","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# NovoMedici, LLC — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-14\n     4→Developer website: https://www.novomedici.com/\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→NovoMedici, LLC is a small EHR vendor based in Ogden, Utah, that develops and sells NovoClinical, a cloud-based electronic health record and practice management platform. The company describes nearly 20 years of research and development preceding the product's launch. NovoMedici is very small — ZoomInfo lists approximately 5–9 employees across the NovoMedici and NovoClinical entities. The company positions NovoClinical as a \"fully integrated EMR system designed by practicing physicians,\" targeting small to mid-sized ambulatory medical practices. The vendor emphasizes a modular, scalable pricing model (\"pay only for what is needed\") and a user interface modeled after traditional paper charts to ease adoption. NovoClinical is cloud-hosted and accessible across devices including tablets and iPads. The company has no publicly noted acquisition history, parent company, or rebranding — it appears to be an independent, bootstrapped operation.\n     9→\n    10→## Product: NovoClinical\n    11→\n    12→CHPL IDs: 10805\n    13→\n    14→### What It Is\n    15→\n    16→NovoClinical is an all-in-one ambulatory EHR and practice management system. It combines clinical documentation, billing/revenue cycle management, scheduling, e-prescribing, patient portal, telemedicine, and chronic care management into a single integrated platform. The certified module (NovoClinical version 1.0, certified 2022-01-31) appears to be the whole product — there is no indication of separate products or platforms. It is certified against a broad set of ONC criteria spanning clinical (a)(1)–(a)(5), (a)(12), (a)(14); care coordination (b)(1)–(b)(3), (b)(10)–(b)(11); patient portal (e)(1); CQMs (c)(1)–(c)(3); public health reporting (f)(1), (f)(2), (f)(5); APIs (g)(7), (g)(9), (g)(10); and direct messaging (h)(1).\n    17→\n    18→### Users & Market\n    19→\n    20→The CHPL metadata describes intended users as \"Providers, Nurses and Medical assistant.\" Third-party review sites describe the target market as small to mid-sized medical practices, including solo practitioners, independent clinics, and multi-provider practices. Supported specialties include general practice, cardiology, immunology, gastroenterology, OB/GYN, pediatrics, and dermatology. The product is priced at $99–$385/provider/month depending on module selection (specific features only vs. EMR only vs. EMR + practice management). No specific customer counts or notable deployments were found in any source. The company does not appear to have significant market share — it has a modest number of reviews on Capterra and other directories (around 30 reviews on FindEMR, with 85% excellent ratings). Users praise customer service and the intuitive interface but note that billing/RCM features could be improved.\n    21→\n    22→### Modules & Functionality\n    23→\n    24→Based on vendor materials, third-party review sites, and the features page, NovoClinical includes the following modules and capabilities:\n    25→\n    26→**Clinical Documentation / EHR:**\n    27→- Charting with customizable templates and reports\n    28→- Voice recognition technology for dictation\n    29→- Decision support (clinical decision support / CPOE — certified (a)(1)–(a)(5))\n    30→- Order and result tracking\n    31→- Problem lists, medication lists, medication allergy lists (certified (a)(1)–(a)(4))\n    32→- Clinical information reconciliation (certified (a)(12))\n    33→- Implantable device list (certified (a)(14))\n    34→\n    35→**E-Prescribing:**\n    36→- Electronic prescribing (e-Rx), implied integration with Surescripts or similar network via API/HL7 integrations described on the features page\n    37→\n    38→**Scheduling & Check-in:**\n    39→- Appointment scheduling\n    40→- Auto check-in via iPad/tablet with automatic EHR syncing\n    41→- Appointment reminders\n    42→\n    43→**Practice Management:**\n    44→- Patient registration and demographic management\n    45→- Check-ins, referrals, and reporting\n    46→- Patient eligibility verification\n    47→\n    48→**Billing & Revenue Cycle Management (RCM):**\n    49→- Medical billing and coding\n    50→- UB-04 billing support\n    51→- Claim scrubbing\n    52→- Durable Medical Equipment (DME) billing\n    53→- Medical accounting\n    54→- Statement generation\n    55→- Credit card payment integration\n    56→- Claims processing and payment collection\n    57→\n    58→**Patient Portal:**\n    59→- Secure patient messaging\n    60→- Access to visit summaries, lab results, and medication details\n    61→- Online appointment scheduling\n    62→- Patient input of demographics and medical history\n    63→- E-signature for documents\n    64→- Offered free with the EHR\n    65→\n    66→**Telemedicine:**\n    67→- Virtual visit capabilities for patients with limited mobility or scheduling constraints\n    68→\n    69→**Chronic Care Management (CCM):**\n    70→- Monitoring and tracking for patients with chronic conditions (diabetes, hypertension, heart disease)\n    71→\n    72→**Communication & Messaging:**\n    73→- Built-in e-fax\n    74→- Text messaging (SMS)\n    75→- Alerts and notifications\n    76→- Task management\n    77→- Direct messaging (certified (h)(1))\n    78→\n    79→**Integrations:**\n    80→- API/HL7 integrations with laboratories, imaging centers, e-prescribing networks\n    81→- Radiology Information Systems (RIS) integration\n    82→- Picture Archiving and Communication Systems (PACS) integration\n    83→- ICD-10 coding support\n    84→\n    85→**Public Health Reporting:**\n    86→- Immunization registry reporting (certified (f)(1))\n    87→- Syndromic surveillance (certified (f)(2))\n    88→- Cancer case reporting (certified (f)(5))\n    89→\n    90→**Interoperability & Data Exchange:**\n    91→- Transitions of care (certified (b)(1)–(b)(3))\n    92→- FHIR API access (certified (g)(7), (g)(9), (g)(10))\n    93→- Patient portal view/download/transmit (certified (e)(1))\n    94→\n    95→### Data & Content\n    96→\n    97→Based on the features described above and the certification criteria, NovoClinical stores and manages the following categories of data:\n    98→\n    99→**Clinical data:** Patient demographics, medical history, problem lists, medication lists, medication allergy lists, implantable device lists, clinical notes/charting, visit summaries, lab orders and results, imaging orders and results (via RIS/PACS integration), vital signs, immunization records.\n   100→\n   101→**Prescribing data:** E-prescriptions, medication history (implied by e-prescribing and medication list features).\n   102→\n   103→**Scheduling and administrative data:** Appointments, patient check-in records, referrals, tasks, alerts/notifications.\n   104→\n   105→**Billing and financial data:** Claims, billing codes (ICD-10, UB-04), payment records, credit card transactions, statements, accounts receivable, DME billing records. Multiple sources confirm billing is built into the platform, not a separate product.\n   106→\n   107→**Patient portal data:** Patient-entered demographics and medical history, secure messages between patients and providers, e-signed documents, appointment requests.\n   108→\n   109→**Telemedicine data:** Virtual visit records (how these are stored — as notes, separate encounters, or otherwise — is not specified in available materials).\n   110→\n   111→**Chronic care management data:** Care plans, monitoring data for chronic conditions (specifics not detailed in available materials).\n   112→\n   113→**Communication records:** E-faxes, text messages, direct messages (via Direct protocol).\n   114→\n   115→**Public health reporting data:** Immunization registries, syndromic surveillance data, cancer case reports.\n   116→\n   117→**Gaps and uncertainties:** The vendor website is relatively sparse on deep technical details. Third-party integration specifics are limited — FindEMR notes the vendor \"has not specified the details about its specific third-party integrations.\" There is no publicly available data dictionary or schema documentation beyond the EHI export format PDF. The exact scope of data stored for telemedicine encounters and chronic care management is not well-documented in publicly available materials. Review sites note some limitations in the RCM module, suggesting it may not be as feature-complete as the clinical side.\n   118→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. The company describes nearly 20 years of research and development preceding the product's launch. NovoMedici is very small — ZoomInfo lists approximately 5–9 employees across the NovoMedici and NovoClinical entities. The company positions NovoClinical as a \"fully integrated EMR system designed by practicing physicians,\" targeting small to mid-sized ambulatory medical practices. The vendor emphasizes a modular, scalable pricing model (\"pay only for what is needed\") and a user interface modeled after traditional paper charts to ease adoption. NovoClinical is cloud-hosted and accessible across devices including tablets and iPads. The company has no publicly noted acquisition history, parent company, or rebranding — it appears to be an independent, bootstrapped operation.\n\n## Product: NovoClinical\n\nCHPL IDs: 10805\n\n### What It Is\n\nNovoClinical is an all-in-one ambulatory EHR and practice management system. It combines clinical documentation, billing/revenue cycle management, scheduling, e-prescribing, patient portal, telemedicine, and chronic care management into a single integrated platform. The certified module (NovoClinical version 1.0, certified 2022-01-31) appears to be the whole product — there is no indication of separate products or platforms. It is certified against a broad set of ONC criteria spanning clinical (a)(1)–(a)(5), (a)(12), (a)(14); care coordination (b)(1)–(b)(3), (b)(10)–(b)(11); patient portal (e)(1); CQMs (c)(1)–(c)(3); public health reporting (f)(1), (f)(2), (f)(5); APIs (g)(7), (g)(9), (g)(10); and direct messaging (h)(1).\n\n### Users & Market\n\nThe CHPL metadata describes intended users as \"Providers, Nurses and Medical assistant.\" Third-party review sites describe the target market as small to mid-sized medical practices, including solo practitioners, independent clinics, and multi-provider practices. Supported specialties include general practice, cardiology, immunology, gastroenterology, OB/GYN, pediatrics, and dermatology. The product is priced at $99–$385/provider/month depending on module selection (specific features only vs. EMR only vs. EMR + practice management). No specific customer counts or notable deployments were found in any source. The company does not appear to have significant market share — it has a modest number of reviews on Capterra and other directories (around 30 reviews on FindEMR, with 85% excellent ratings). Users praise customer service and the intuitive interface but note that billing/RCM features could be improved.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on vendor materials, third-party review sites, and the features page, NovoClinical includes the following modules and capabilities:\n\n**Clinical Documentation / EHR:**\n- Charting with customizable templates and reports\n- Voice recognition technology for dictation\n- Decision support (clinical decision support / CPOE — certified (a)(1)–(a)(5))\n- Order and result tracking\n- Problem lists, medication lists, medication allergy lists (certified (a)(1)–(a)(4))\n- Clinical information reconciliation (certified (a)(12))\n- Implantable device list (certified (a)(14))\n\n**E-Prescribing:**\n- Electronic prescribing (e-Rx), implied integration with Surescripts or similar network via API/HL7 integrations described on the features page\n\n**Scheduling & Check-in:**\n- Appointment scheduling\n- Auto check-in via iPad/tablet with automatic EHR syncing\n- Appointment reminders\n\n**Practice Management:**\n- Patient registration and demographic management\n- Check-ins, referrals, and reporting\n- Patient eligibility verification\n\n**Billing & Revenue Cycle Management (RCM):**\n- Medical billing and coding\n- UB-04 billing support\n- Claim scrubbing\n- Durable Medical Equipment (DME) billing\n- Medical accounting\n- Statement generation\n- Credit card payment integration\n- Claims processing and payment collection\n\n**Patient Portal:**\n- Secure patient messaging\n- Access to visit summaries, lab results, and medication details\n- Online appointment scheduling\n- Patient input of demographics and medical history\n- E-signature for documents\n- Offered free with the EHR\n\n**Telemedicine:**\n- Virtual visit capabilities for patients with limited mobility or scheduling constraints\n\n**Chronic Care Management (CCM):**\n- Monitoring and tracking for patients with chronic conditions (diabetes, hypertension, heart disease)\n\n**Communication & Messaging:**\n- Built-in e-fax\n- Text messaging (SMS)\n- Alerts and notifications\n- Task management\n- Direct messaging (certified (h)(1))\n\n**Integrations:**\n- API/HL7 integrations with laboratories, imaging centers, e-prescribing networks\n- Radiology Information Systems (RIS) integration\n- Picture Archiving and Communication Systems (PACS) integration\n- ICD-10 coding support\n\n**Public Health Reporting:**\n- Immunization registry reporting (certified (f)(1))\n- Syndromic surveillance (certified (f)(2))\n- Cancer case reporting (certified (f)(5))\n\n**Interoperability & Data Exchange:**\n- Transitions of care (certified (b)(1)–(b)(3))\n- FHIR API access (certified (g)(7), (g)(9), (g)(10))\n- Patient portal view/download/transmit (certified (e)(1))\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the features described above and the certification criteria, NovoClinical stores and manages the following categories of data:\n\n**Clinical data:** Patient demographics, medical history, problem lists, medication lists, medication allergy lists, implantable device lists, clinical notes/charting, visit summaries, lab orders and results, imaging orders and results (via RIS/PACS integration), vital signs, immunization records.\n\n**Prescribing data:** E-prescriptions, medication history (implied by e-prescribing and medication list features).\n\n**Scheduling and administrative data:** Appointments, patient check-in records, referrals, tasks, alerts/notifications.\n\n**Billing and financial data:** Claims, billing codes (ICD-10, UB-04), payment records, credit card transactions, statements, accounts receivable, DME billing records. Multiple sources confirm billing is built into the platform, not a separate product.\n\n**Patient portal data:** Patient-entered demographics and medical history, secure messages between patients and providers, e-signed documents, appointment requests.\n\n**Telemedicine data:** Virtual visit records (how these are stored — as notes, separate encounters, or otherwise — is not specified in available materials).\n\n**Chronic care management data:** Care plans, monitoring data for chronic conditions (specifics not detailed in available materials).\n\n**Communication records:** E-faxes, text messages, direct messages (via Direct protocol).\n\n**Public health reporting data:** Immunization registries, syndromic surveillance data, cancer case reports.\n\n**Gaps and uncertainties:** The vendor website is relatively sparse on deep technical details. Third-party integration specifics are limited — FindEMR notes the vendor \"has not specified the details about its specific third-party integrations.\" There is no publicly available data dictionary or schema documentation beyond the EHI export format PDF. The exact scope of data stored for telemedicine encounters and chronic care management is not well-documented in publicly available materials. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01EM4dNntMop3LatbMWYUNQP","type":"tool_result","content":"Novoclinical Data Export Format\nC-CDA (Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture) – Each patient will have a C-CDA document in the\nexported data.\nCSV – Comma separated value, used for patient demography, Appointments.\n\nData export can be done by clinic administrators by navigating to Communication > Data Export\nThe below page opens and let you choose the specific patient export or group export of all or multiple\npatients. Once exported administrator will be able to export the data in a ZIP file which will contact the\nCCD-A, CSV file.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"49feb525-d6e0-4bf6-a146-2c8e7af0040a","uuid":"fcc824a3-51f8-426f-9fce-b6cd7da87a08","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"Novoclinical Data Export Format\nC-CDA (Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture) – Each patient will have a C-CDA document in the\nexported data.\nCSV – Comma separated value, used for patient demography, Appointments.\n\nData export can be done by clinic administrators by navigating to Communication > Data Export\nThe below page opens and let you choose the specific patient export or group export of all or multiple\npatients. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01396T1hAF7nmBXgFVwCDmA5","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_016aRStJjWoPnJXVrxp1Dqe7","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/novomedici-llc/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# NovoMedici, LLC — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-14\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://s3.amazonaws.com/novoclinical.miscellaneous/Novoclinical+Data+Export+Format.pdf\n- CHPL IDs: 10805\n- Product: NovoClinical v1.0 (certified 2022-01-31)\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n**1. Initial probe of the registered URL:**\n```bash\ncurl -sI -L \"https://s3.amazonaws.com/novoclinical.miscellaneous/Novoclinical+Data+Export+Format.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n```\nReturned HTTP 200, Content-Type: application/pdf, Content-Length: 129544 bytes. Direct PDF download from Amazon S3. Last-Modified: 2023-10-08.\n\n**2. Downloaded the PDF:**\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://s3.amazonaws.com/novoclinical.miscellaneous/Novoclinical+Data+Export+Format.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o downloads/Novoclinical-Data-Export-Format.pdf\n```\nVerified with `file` command: confirmed as \"PDF document, version 1.7, 1 page(s)\". Created with Microsoft Word for Microsoft 365 on 2023-10-07.\n\n**3. Extracted text and rendered the PDF visually:**\nThe PDF is a single page. It contains:\n- A title: \"Novoclinical Data Export Format\"\n- Two bullet points describing the export formats (C-CDA and CSV)\n- Navigation instructions for performing the export\n- A screenshot of the export interface in NovoClinical\n\n**4. Checked the vendor's mandatory disclosures page:**\nNavigated to https://www.novomedici.com/meaningful-use/ in a browser. The page lists several links:\n- \"Novoclinical V1 Mandatory Disclosures and Costs\" — regulatory disclosure PDF, not EHI-specific\n- \"Application access\" / \"Patient selection\" — (g)(7) documentation\n- \"NovoClinical API terms of use\" — API terms\n- Footer link \"EMR Data Export\" — points to the same PDF already downloaded\n\n**5. Checked the API documents page:**\nNavigated to https://www.novomedici.com/api-documents/. This page only contains FHIR API base URLs and Smart-on-FHIR configuration links — this is (g)(10) API documentation, not EHI export documentation.\n\n**6. Conclusion:** The entire EHI export documentation is the single one-page PDF.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe EHI export documentation consists of a single one-page PDF that describes the export mechanism in three short sentences:\n\n> **C-CDA (Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture)** — Each patient will have a C-CDA document in the exported data.\n>\n> **CSV** — Comma separated value, used for patient demography, Appointments.\n>\n> Data export can be done by clinic administrators by navigating to Communication > Data Export. The below page opens and let you choose the specific patient export or group export of all or multiple patients. Once exported administrator will be able to export the data in a ZIP file which will contact the CCD-A, CSV file.\n\nThe PDF includes a screenshot of the export interface, which shows:\n- A \"Data Export\" page with a \"Patient Export\" tab selected\n- Patient selection fields (patient name, date range options)\n- An \"Export Data\" button and a \"Reset\" button\n- The NovoClinical navigation bar showing modules: Clinical, Billing, Reporting, Reports, Admin, Templates, Scheduler\n\nThat is the entirety of the documentation. There is no data dictionary, no field-level documentation, no schema, no sample files, no format specification for the CSV files, and no description of what C-CDA sections or templates are used.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nBased on the product research, NovoClinical is an all-in-one ambulatory EHR and practice management system that stores:\n- Clinical data (charting, problem lists, medications, allergies, labs, vitals, immunizations, implantable devices, clinical notes)\n- Prescribing data (e-prescriptions, medication history)\n- Scheduling data (appointments, check-ins, referrals)\n- Billing/RCM data (claims, billing codes, payments, DME billing, statements)\n- Patient portal data (messages, patient-entered history, e-signed documents)\n- Telemedicine data (virtual visit records)\n- Chronic care management data (care plans, monitoring)\n- Communication records (e-faxes, text messages, direct messages)\n- Public health reporting data (immunization registries, syndromic surveillance, cancer case reports)\n\nThe export documentation explicitly mentions only:\n- **C-CDA documents**: These would cover a standard clinical summary — problems, medications, allergies, lab results, vitals, immunizations, procedures, and possibly some clinical notes. However, C-CDA is a clinical summary standard; it does not cover the full breadth of data an EHR stores.\n- **CSV for \"patient demography, Appointments\"**: Demographics and appointment scheduling data only.\n\n**Clearly missing or unaddressed domains:**\n- **Billing and financial data** — claims, charges, payments, statements, coding. This is a core function of the product (it's marketed as \"Medical Billing Software for Small Business\") and there is no mention of billing data in the export.\n- **Clinical notes beyond C-CDA summaries** — progress notes, H&P, specialty-specific documentation. C-CDA may carry some notes, but the documentation doesn't specify which sections are populated.\n- **Prescribing data** — e-prescribing history beyond what C-CDA might include.\n- **Patient portal data** — secure messages, patient-entered forms, e-signatures.\n- **Telemedicine records** — virtual visit documentation.\n- **Chronic care management data** — care plans, monitoring records.\n- **Communication records** — faxes, text messages, direct messages.\n- **Referrals and care coordination data**.\n- **Custom templates and specialty-specific clinical data**.\n- **Documents, images, and attachments** in the patient record.\n- **Lab and imaging orders** (as distinct from results in C-CDA).\n\nThe export appears to be a narrow clinical summary (C-CDA) plus basic demographics and scheduling (CSV), covering perhaps 20-30% of what the product actually stores. This is a significant gap for a (b)(10) EHI export requirement.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses two formats:\n- **C-CDA**: A recognized HL7 standard for clinical document exchange. However, the documentation does not specify which C-CDA document type (CCD, Discharge Summary, etc.), which template versions, or which optional sections are populated. Without this information, a recipient cannot know what data to expect.\n- **CSV**: For demographics and appointments. No column definitions, delimiter specifications, encoding details, or sample files are provided.\n\nThe output is delivered as a ZIP file containing C-CDA XML and CSV files.\n\nThe format choice is partially appropriate — C-CDA handles standard clinical data reasonably well, but it cannot represent billing records, custom clinical forms, communications, or many other data domains the product stores. A true (b)(10) export would need additional formats (database dump, additional CSV files for billing tables, etc.) to cover the full designated record set.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation is extremely minimal — arguably the bare minimum that could be called \"documentation.\" Specific deficiencies:\n\n- **No data dictionary**: There are no field definitions for either the C-CDA content or the CSV files.\n- **No schema or format specification**: The CSV columns are not defined. The C-CDA template constraints are not documented.\n- **No sample files**: No example exports are provided.\n- **No value sets or coded field documentation**: No indication of what coding systems are used or how coded values map.\n- **No relationship documentation**: No description of how the C-CDA and CSV files relate to each other.\n- **No import guidance**: A developer could not implement an import of this data based on this documentation alone.\n\nA developer receiving this export would have to reverse-engineer the file formats entirely from actual export files.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: The documentation operates at the format level only (\"C-CDA\" and \"CSV\"). There is no table-level, field-level, or element-level documentation.\n- **Value sets**: Not documented.\n- **Relationships**: Not documented.\n- **Versioning**: The PDF has no version number. The Last-Modified date on S3 is October 2023.\n\nThis is among the most minimal EHI export documentation possible — a single page that names two file formats and shows a screenshot of how to trigger the export. It does not meet the informational needs of anyone trying to understand, verify, or use the exported data.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://s3.amazonaws.com/novoclinical.miscellaneous/Novoclinical+Data+Export+Format.pdf\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- The mandatory disclosures page (https://www.novomedici.com/meaningful-use/) uses Brotli compression that prevented direct curl text extraction; browser rendering was needed to read the page. Initial probe of the registered URL:**\n```bash\ncurl -sI -L \"https://s3.amazonaws.com/novoclinical.miscellaneous/Novoclinical+Data+Export+Format.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n```\nReturned HTTP 200, Content-Type: application/pdf, Content-Length: 129544 bytes.
